Frontier-class AI coding models are now open-weight and free to deploy. Two dropped in the same week.

Moonshot AI open-sourced Kimi K2.7 Code — a trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model purpose-built for agentic coding, outperforming its predecessor while using fewer reasoning tokens. In the same week, Poolside released Laguna M.1 under Apache 2.0: a 225B-parameter sparse model with a 256K context window that runs on well-provisioned workstations.

For business and engineering leaders, this changes the math on AI-powered development. Frontier code generation no longer requires expensive API subscriptions or dependence on proprietary platforms. These models can be self-hosted, fine-tuned on your own data, and deployed with zero per-token costs.

The practical upside is significant: full control over your AI coding infrastructure, data privacy by default, and the ability to customize for your specific engineering workflows. The trade-off is that you need the internal capability to evaluate, deploy, and maintain these systems.
